title: How to Live to Be 194 Years Old - Nautilus
gist: A brief teaser on Jonathan, an Aldabra giant tortoise brought from the Seychelles to St. Helena in 1882 and estimated to be 194 years old, framed as a subject for longevity research.

insights.claim: Jonathan, an Aldabra giant tortoise shipped from the Seychelles to St. Helena in 1882, was estimated to be 50 on arrival based on his size, making him about 194 years old.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Extremely long-lived species are natural models for longevity science.
insights.quote: Based on Jonathan’s size when he arrived in St. Helena, he was already 50 years old, making him now 194 years old.

insights.claim: Four Aldabra giant tortoises were captured by British officials in 1882 and transported nearly 3,000 nautical miles as a gift to St. Helena governor Sir William Grey-Wilson, who died a century ago while Jonathan survives.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Contextual history illustrating lifespans that outlast human generations.

insights.claim: The article frames Jonathan as a continuing source of insight into tortoise longevity, describing him as a gift that keeps on giving.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Signals ongoing scientific interest in the biology of long-lived reptiles.
insights.quote: And Jonathan is a gift that keeps on giving.
